newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila said nearing deal on Eurodollar notes.
newsitem.headline: Manila said nearing deal on Eurodollar notes.

text.p: The Philippine central bank is set to close a deal with a foreign financial institution to underwrite Eurodollar notes, Bankers Association of the Philippines president Deogracias Vistan said.

"Some of the foreign banks have offered some pretty extensive and some pretty large amount of credit facility. And I think one of them is nearing an agreement," Vistan told journalists on Thursday night.
Central bank officials declined to comment, although central bank managing director Amando Tetangco earlier told reporters the bank was looking at the various offers.

Several foreign financial institutions have approached the central bank to underwrite short-term notes to help beef up its international reserves which were depleted when it launched a massive, albeit futile, defence of the peso against speculators in June and July.

Among the banks which have offered to underwrite are Bank of Tokyo, Goldman Sachs, Salomon Brothers, Merrill Lynch, Nomura Securities, ING Barings, JP Morgan, ABN Amro, Chase Manhattan and Deustche Morgan Grenfell.
The central bank launched $550 million worth of Yankee bonds last June, but the proceeds were used to defend the peso, a central bank official said.
